name: Breadth-First Search
description: Graph traversal algorithm that explores all vertices at the current depth level before moving to vertices at the next depth level. Uses a queue to track the frontier of exploration.
aim: To traverse or search a graph level by level starting from a source node, visiting all neighbors of the current node before moving deeper. Guarantees finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs.
howItWorks: Start at the source node, mark it as visited, and add it to a queue
While the queue is not empty, dequeue the front node
Process the current node (print it, record it, etc.)
For each unvisited neighbor of the current node: mark as visited and enqueue
Repeat until the queue is empty — all reachable nodes have been visited

time.bestCase: Always O(V+E) — must visit all vertices and edges
time.averageCase: V = vertices, E = edges — each visited once
time.worstCase: Dense graph with many edges still O(V+E)

complexity.spaceDescription: Queue and visited array each hold at most V elements

realWorld: Shortest path in unweighted graphs — GPS navigation, network routing
Social networks — finding people within N degrees of connection
Web crawlers — discovering linked pages level by level
Puzzle solving — finding minimum moves in games like sliding puzzles
Network broadcast — sending messages to all nodes within k hops
whenToUse: Finding shortest path in an unweighted graph
Exploring nodes closest to source first
Checking if a graph is bipartite
Finding all nodes within a given distance
alternatives: Use DFS for topological sort, cycle detection, or path existence checks
Use Dijkstra's for shortest path in weighted graphs
Use A* when a heuristic can guide the search (e.g., grids, maps)
Use Bidirectional BFS to halve the search space for source-to-target queries
